analysis: Examined the two changed files. (1) ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift: the only changed behavior is in unloadModel (~line 1191). persistLoadedModelSet() is now skipped when servingDrain.owner == .addonHold, so an add-on hold's temporary unload keeps the persisted serving set for startup preload. This only affects local availability and preload planning. It adds no plaintext exposure, key handling, cache-at-rest change (T-041) or attestation change. The weight-hash TOCTOU bracket and load paths in the surrounding head text are unchanged context. (2) ProviderLoop+PlannedDisconnect.swift (patch only; the excerpt is marked incomplete, but the full patch was supplied): waitForSafeDisconnect gains underAddonHold with a fenceAllowed() check before and after the inflight drain, so a non-reconnect disconnect is refused while an add-on hold owns the drain. ownsPlannedReconnect admits .reconnect or .addonHold for the reconnect loop. The hold keeps ownership, so the fresh registration cannot reopen admission. Added reassertAddonHoldAfterReconnect() and resumeAfterAddonHold(), which convert the release into a reconnect or planned reconnect if a barrier or retirement reconnect is pending. Admission stays closed during a reconnect under the hold, which is fail-closed. No authorization, App Attest grant (T-053) or connection-binding logic is touched directly. Open integration questions: the implementations of servingDrain.resumeAddonHold, reassertAddonHoldAfterReconnect and beginServingDrain(owner:) are outside the supplied evidence. The next pass should verify that a reconnect under the hold cannot reopen admission before the new registration and grant (TB-002/TB-011 stale-authorization concern, T-053). It should also confirm the hold cannot deadlock draining or availability (T-010). No concrete regression is visible in the supplied lines.
